A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same point-cloud synthesis framework despite retitling and substantial revision. All 13 pages of v1 and 17 pages of v2, including their appendices, provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures sufficient for comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original ShapeNet reconstruction and generation experiments, MNIST and synthetic-manifold rotation experiments, and test-set reconstruction analyses in Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 reports original ShapeNet reconstruction, generation, compression, loss-ablation, and direct-optimization results in Sections 4.1–4.5 and the appendices.

M1.justification: Beyond renaming ECT to IPT, v2 replaces coordinate-plane direction sampling with sphere sampling and the four-layer MLP with a 1D convolutional encoder followed by fully connected layers. It replaces directional-density KL regularization with an IPT-MSE-based joint loss, revises the VAE architecture, and introduces learned downsampling and direct coordinate optimization.

E1.justification: The three ShapeNet classes remain, but v1's point-cloud MNIST and synthetic-manifold datasets, including rotated reconstruction and cross-manifold interpolation, are removed. V2 adds a distinct compression/upsampling task that reduces 2048-point ShapeNet inputs to 256 points before reconstructing them.

E2.justification: V2 adds Canonical VAE to the reconstruction comparison and PVD and LION to generation comparisons. SetVAE was already evaluated for generation in v1. Uniform subsampling becomes a compression comparator, while the random-rotation comparator disappears with the removed equivariance experiments.

E3.justification: V2 removes normalized/original cross-evaluation and the separate test-set/IQR protocol. VAE latent dimensionality changes from 256 to 32, 64, or 150 by class, and new compression and resolution/scale-sweep protocols appear. The written CD formula changes from squared Euclidean distances in v1 Equation 1 to unsquared norms in v2 Equation 8; whether underlying scores were recomputed accordingly is not established.

E4.justification: V2 adds CD-only, IPT-only, and joint-loss ablations in Table 2, resolution and sigmoid-scale sensitivity experiments in Appendix C, and compression transfer analyses. V1's rotation-equivariance experiments and detailed reconstruction-outlier analyses are removed. ShapeNet interpolation remains, but MNIST and manifold interpolation cases disappear.

E5.justification: V1 explicitly reports averaging reconstruction results across 10 runs, distinguishes variability of means from per-shape variability, and includes critical-difference significance analyses. V2 removes these explanations and analyses while retaining unexplained ± entries in Tables 1 and C.1. This establishes a reporting change, not an actual change in run counts.

E6.justification: Proposed-model results are substantially replaced: original-data airplane EMD is 4.85 for v1's ECT-MLP and 1.44 for v2's IP-Encoder, under changed models and protocols. PointFlow's chair-CD entry also changes from 6.94 to 10.43. V2 adds generation MMD/COV, compression, ablation, and optimization results, while removing normalized, test-set, and rotation results.

T1.justification: V1 defines the ECT and derives a directional-density KL loss without supplying original proofs. V2 adds injectivity and rational-interpolation theorems, metric and additivity lemmas, and their proofs in Appendix F. Its mathematical loss formulation and written Chamfer-distance definition also change substantially.

C1.justification: V2 makes its own theoretical guarantees and out-of-distribution processing without retraining headline contributions. V1's main claim of learning rotational equivariance through augmentation is removed. Efficient generation and smooth interpolation remain central, but the contribution shifts toward a theoretically justified descriptor and compression/upsampling capabilities.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations of complementary density/detail losses, gradient failures as sigmoid scale varies, and transfer to compressed inputs. It introduces a mass-transport interpretation of interpolation and finite-direction caveats. V1's discussions of scale confounding, outlier-driven performance differences, and the model's comparatively large parameter count are removed.

D1.justification: V2 adds tensor-shape and network schematics in Appendix E, encoder epoch counts, a VAE annealing schedule, and direct-optimization learning-rate milestones. It removes v1's general Adam learning rates, parameter-count comparison, and promise to release code and configurations. Training-time disclosures also change; actual code availability cannot be determined from either PDF.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning around image-based reconstruction, Fourier-feature representations, and contemporary point-cloud generators while explicitly retaining the IPT–ECT relationship. New references include Cheng, Fahim, Tancik, Xu, Zeng, and Zhou; Abramson and Demšar are removed. These accompany substantive positioning changes, not merely bibliography reformatting.

P1.justification: The title, terminology, introduction, and methodological exposition are extensively rewritten around a self-contained point-cloud formulation. Related work becomes a separate section, reconstruction and generation receive separate experimental sections, and metrics move to an appendix. The appendix organization is substantially replaced and expanded.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout, with restructured tables and redrawn point-cloud illustrations. Critical-difference, rotation, and outlier displays disappear; loss, compression, and optimization tables and IPT-overview/downsampling figures are added. The timing table also loses its parameter-count column.

improvement.justification: V2's newer baselines and loss/resolution ablations provide broader, more diagnostic empirical evidence. However, it removes v1's uncertainty explanations and test-set outlier analysis. Its new Appendix F proof assumes n+1 linearly independent directions in R^n, which is impossible, and the interpolation proof treats repeated set unions as preserving multiplicity despite the stated set formulation. These empirical gains and losses in evidential and mathematical reliability prevent a confident net quality judgment.
